1: Chapter 1: A Visitor on a Rainy Night

It had been raining in Qingshi for three days straight. Lin Xiaoyu closed the door of the medicine shop and lit the last lamp. She was twenty-two this year, and since her father's death she had kept this little shop going on her own.
"Is anyone there?" a man's voice came from outside the door.

Lin Xiaoyu hesitated, then opened the door anyway. A young man stood there, soaked to the bone, his left hand clamped over his right arm, blood seeping between his fingers. He said his name was Chen Ziming, and that he had come from the provincial capital.
"I need this bandaged," Chen Ziming said quietly. "I can pay. Will a hundred and twenty yuan be enough?"

She didn't take his money. She only had him sit down beside the counter, then turned to fetch gauze and medicinal liquor. The wound wasn't deep, but it was long, as if it had been opened with a knife. As she cleaned it, she asked him how he had been hurt.

Chen Ziming was silent for a long time before he said, "I ran into some men on the road. They wanted a letter I was carrying." He took an oil-paper packet from inside his coat and set it on the table. "This letter has to reach Baiyun before May 18."

Lin Xiaoyu glanced out the window. Baiyun was up in the mountains, forty li from Qingshi, and mountain roads were hardest to travel in the rain. She thought of what her father used to say: when you save someone, you save them all the way.
"I'll take you up the mountain first thing tomorrow," she said. "Tonight you can sleep in the back room."
2: It was still dark when Lin Xiaoyu woke Chen Ziming. She slung a bamboo basket on her back, packed with dry rations, herbs and an old umbrella. Chen Ziming's arm had improved a little, but his face was still pale.
Halfway up the mountain they met an old woodcutter, Zhou Dashan. He knew Lin Xiaoyu, and asked her with a smile where she was off to so early.
"To Baiyun Temple, to deliver medicine," Lin Xiaoyu answered. She said nothing about the letter.
Zhou Dashan glanced at Chen Ziming and lowered his voice. "Yesterday evening three strangers were asking around the town gate about a wounded young man. You two be careful."

Chen Ziming's face went paler still. Lin Xiaoyu thanked the old man and led Chen Ziming off the main road onto a narrow trail that only herb gatherers knew. It was narrow and slippery; she walked in front, setting every step down firm and sure.

At noon the rain finally stopped. The mountain mist slowly thinned, and far off the roof of Baiyun Temple came into view. A nun stood at the temple gate — Zhao Qiuyue, who received the temple's guests.
Zhao Qiuyue took the oil-paper packet, checked the red seal on the fold, and nodded. "Our master has waited 2 years for this letter," she said. "Thank you for your trouble."
On the way back, Chen Ziming said to Lin Xiaoyu, "I owe you my life." Lin Xiaoyu smiled. "Then next time you come to Qingshi, you can fix the roof of my medicine shop for me."
